title: Permutations II
statement: The list may contain duplicate values. Return all UNIQUE permutations in any order.

hints.1_question: Plain permutations would generate identical lists when equal values are swapped. How can you avoid choosing 'the same value' twice at the same position?
hints.2_nudge: Sort the array. At each position skip a value if it equals the previous one and the previous one is not currently in use.
hints.3_big_hint: Sort first. In the loop: if i > 0 and nums[i] == nums[i-1] and not used[i-1]: continue.

known_bugs.name: no duplicate handling
known_bugs.code:
def permuteUnique(nums):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    res, cur = [], []
    used = [False] * len(nums)
    def bt():
        if len(cur) == len(nums):
            res.append(cur[:])
            return
        for i in range(len(nums)):
            if used[i]:
                continue
            used[i] = True
            cur.append(nums[i])
            bt()
            cur.pop()
            used[i] = False
    bt()
    return res
known_bugs.followup: For [1, 1, 2] how many times is [1, 1, 2] produced?

known_bugs.name: skips every value equal to its left neighbour (ignores whether it is in use)
known_bugs.followup: For [1, 1] your code produces no permutation at all. The second 1 may be needed once the first 1 is already in the current permutation - when is it right to skip it?

known_bugs.name: forgets to sort first
known_bugs.followup: Your skip rule compares neighbouring positions. In [2, 1, 2] are the two 2s neighbours?

followups: Why must equal values be used in left-to-right order?
Could a counter (value -> count) replace the used array?
